To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we measured atmospheric Ar and Ne trapped at mantle depths in a coesite-bearing eclogite and that this is the first study to document when atmospheric gases were trapped in ultramafic rocks exhumed to the Earth’s atmosphere from the mantle.
atmospheric Ar and He were trapped in phngite and omphactie formed during UHP metamorphic conditions and that the 40Ar/36Ar age of phngite is the timing of crystallisation at UHP conditions.
atmospheric Ar and atmospheric Ne were trapped in UHP minerals and returned to the Earth’s atmosphere by forearc recycling.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fate of atmospheric noble gases in subducting slabs.
the fate of atmospheric gases in subduction zones, and we provide the first evidence, to our knowledge that atmospheric Ar and He were trapped in minerals formed at UHP metamorphic conditions.
the return of atmospheric noble gases to the Earth’s atmosphere by subduction processes and the role of forearc recycling in the global cycling of atmospheric noble gases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the flux of atmospheric noble gases into the mantle through forearc recycling is greater than previously thought and may have a greater impact on the noble gases in the mantle than previously thought.

the flux of atmospheric noble gases entering the deep Earth and returning to the Earth’s atmosphere can only be fully realized by measuring the abundances of noble gases trapped in UHP rocks exhumed in forearcs.
atmospheric noble gas recycling through forearc recycling can return atmospheric Ar and Ne trapped at mantle depths to the earth’s surface in exhumed rocks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the atmospheric noble gas trapped in exhumated UHP metamorphic rocks is a viable mechanism by which atmospheric noble gas is returned to the surface.
atmospheric Ar and atmospheric Ne were returned from mantle depths by forearc recycling.
forearc recycling provides a viable mechanism for the return of atmospheric Ar to the Earth’s atmosphere.
The main takeaway from our work is that
atmospheric Ar and He are recycled to the Earth’s atmosphere in forearcs and are trapped in minerals during exhumation of UHP metamorphic rocks from depths >100 km.
atmospheric Ar and atmospheric Ne can be trapped in phengitic micas and in omphacitic clinopyroxenes crystallized at mantle depths during UHP metamorphic processes.
atmospheric noble gases are returned to the Earth’s atmosphere through forearc recycling.
